text:
SRE-bot: INCIDENT CREATED - routing-service tail latency surge detected, streaming stalls and increased 5xxs. paging: @maria (oncall). Incident ID INC-4299
Maria (oncall): ack. seeing p95 ~ 240ms, p99 ~ 1.3s, streaming stall percentage ~4.2%. multiple customers reporting streaming interruptions (NimbusData, PaperclipAI). grabbing logs.
Akshay: initial glance at routing weight tables shows a suspicious concentration. rolling-affinity v2 was promoted yesterday. I see many micro-weights assigned which might be colliding in the selector.
Jess: router logs show repeated stream resets to the same shard id. sample lines:
```
[router] 2026-03-15T05:02:11Z POST /v1/stream id=cid-99 upstream=shard-42 status=200 stream-reset=1 latency_ms=1389
[model-proxy] 2026-03-15T05:02:11Z shard-42 queue=410 active=420
```
This looks like queue buildup on shard-42.
Carter (night-oncall): I'm in. which regions most impacted?
Akshay: us-west-2 and eu-central show disproportionate hit-rate to shard-42 and shard-7. weight snapshot (excerpt):
```
shard-42: 0.00009
shard-7: 0.00010
shard-3: 0.99981
```
Selector normalization uses a float->int floor which seems to bias mapping for certain prefixes; when many tiny weights exist, hashing modulo maps them to same low-id bucket. I can reproduce locally.
Maria (oncall): mitigation options: (A) immediate rollback of rolling-affinity v2 to v1 (global), (B) apply emergency weight floor config (treat weights < 0.001 as 0) and re-normalize, (C) route-streams to bypass pool (force round-robin) for affected routes. Which gives fastest relief?
Jess: canary rollback might take longer. emergency config floor is quickest. Ops-Runner can push config fast.
Ops-Runner: I can push a config patch in ~4 mins. ready on go.
Akshay: I'll assemble the config patch now — minimal change: treat tiny weights as zero and re-normalize across remaining shards.
SRE-bot: config-push started (cfg-98890) by Akshay. expect propagation ~40-50s per zone.
Maria (oncall): pushing Ops-Runner to scale streaming pool preemptively +2 replicas while patch propagates.
Ops-Runner: scaling streaming-pool from 10 -> 12.
Jess: canary nodes show p99 drop from ~1.3s -> 700ms. queue lengths on shard-42 drop from 410 -> 90. Good sign.
SRE-bot: config-push rolled to 60% routers.
Maria (oncall): global p95 now 210ms, p99 ~710ms, streaming stalls ~1.1%. improvement but still above SLO. Carter, take ownership for steady-state monitoring. I'll handoff.
Carter (night-oncall): taking it. summary: emergency weight-floor applied; observe p99 and streaming stalls for 30m. run `redis-cli -h routing-store HGETALL weights:affinity:v2` and identify values < 0.001. run `scripts/hotmap.sh --window=10m` to produce hotkey map.
Carter (night-oncall): hotmap shows shard-42 receiving ~58% of certain prefix hashes.
Akshay: root cause hypothesis: selector normalization rounding bug causes many tiny weights to be represented similarly in the integer hashing domain, leading to mapping collisions and hot partitions. Repro steps and unit test added.
Jess: action: open rollback PR if config patch doesn't finish improving within 15m. Also capture log buffer for 10m window for postmortem.
Olivia (pm): customer impact: NimbusData claims ~12% sessions affected; we should notify customers on affected list and offer mitigation timeline. prepping comms.
Maria (oncall): assign tasks: @Akshay to open PR with selector fix + tests, @Jess to run stress tests against fixed selector in staging, @Carter to draft incident notification and post to #incidents-notify, @Ops-Runner to keep scaling plan ready.
Akshay: created PR https://git.company/repo/pulls/1430 with unit tests and changelog. requesting expedited review. will also add configuration assertion to reject configs with >30% total weight in micro-weight shards.
SRE-bot: EVENT: mitigation_applied by Akshay at 2765439999.
Carter (night-oncall): current metrics: 30m rolling p99 ~ 640ms, p95 205ms, streaming stalls 0.9%. Still above p99 SLO of 500ms. will monitor for 1h then re-evaluate rollback.
Maria (oncall): leaving pager. Carter you're primary. escalate to oncall lead if p99 > 800ms for 15m.
Carter (night-oncall): ack. posting interim incident note to #incidents-notify in 8m.
Jess: note for postmortem: include timeline of config propagation across regions (we saw ~50s lag per zone) which impacted how fast canary improvement translated to global SLOs.
Olivia (pm): scheduling follow-up with Support & Solutions at 09:00 UTC tomorrow to coordinate customer outreach.
Akshay: additional temporary measure: add selector defensive code to treat weights <0.0005 as 0 and add telemetry to flag when >5% of config entries are micro-weights. will include in PR.
Ops-Runner: scaled streaming pool +2 completed.
SRE-bot: Pager cleared by Maria.
Carter (night-oncall): marking incident mitigated for now. will keep monitoring and prepare postmortem draft. adding backlog items: full rollback exercise, more robust selector tests, telemetry for micro-weight configs.
Maria (oncall): great work team. keep an eye on customer tickets and confirm any required credits or remediation.
